A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Neural Logic Networks work. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including the image-based rule diagrams.

before.justification: v1 reports original tabular classification results, Boolean-network discovery experiments in Appendix D.1, and simulations comparing independence assumptions in Appendix B.1.3.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds a merged RRL medical comparison and NSL-KDD classification and rule-transfer experiments.

M1.justification: Section 4 adds a binary-to-multiclass adaptation: copy learned rules to the new classes, introduce a normal-class bias, then prune and readjust biases. This extends the procedure using existing components; the core NLN architecture, objectives, rule resets, and standard training pipeline remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds cybersecurity coverage through NSL-KDD binary anomaly detection and five-class classification, including testing on 16 attack types unseen in training. This introduces a new domain and distribution-shift scenario while retaining the earlier tabular, Boolean-network, and simulation coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds LAD as a reported comparator for NSL-KDD in Table 7 and adds merged/pruned RRL to the kidney case study, which previously examined only the merged NLN. The original tabular and Boolean-network comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include NSL-KDD's separate 125,973-sample training and 22,544-sample test sets, binary-to-multiclass adaptation, and training/test/full-data F1 reporting. Appendix D.2.1 adds a medical RRL procedure using loss-based pruning followed by F1-based pruning. The existing cross-validation settings remain unchanged; revised RRL table values alone do not establish rerunning those experiments.

E4.justification: The kidney case gains a comparison with a simplified RRL model and its individual risk factors. The industrial application adds analysis of class composition within learned rules, changes after transfer in Figure 8, and all 24 binary rules in Appendix D.3.1. These substantially extend the interpretability and transfer analyses; the earlier independence simulation and Boolean-rule case studies are retained.

E5.justification: The repeated-evaluation information is unchanged, including two repeats of five-fold cross-validation for Boolean-network discovery. v3 introduces no new seed reporting, uncertainty intervals, error bars, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 4–5 revise RRL results: tic-tac-toe mean rule count changes from 412.8 to 313.6 and recovered rules from 87.5% to 75.0%. Table 3 classification scores and Appendix D.1 results remain unchanged. New results include the 13-rule medical RRL model and NSL-KDD binary test F1 of 81.37% for NLN versus 84.78% for LAD; the transferred 17-rule NLN achieves 60.86% multiclass test F1.

T1.justification: Section 2.3 changes the example's stated relationship from B being equal to the DNF to B being implied by it, explicitly describing a sufficient condition. This is a limited revision of the logical relationship. The displayed rule equations, NLN probability formulas, independence assumptions, and Appendix B derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list extend the demonstrated applications from medicine to medicine and industry. The conclusion additionally claims demonstrated binary-to-multiclass rule transfer. The principal contributions concerning probabilistic modeling, negation, biases, factorized rules, and learning remain intact.

C2.justification: v3 adds targeted qualifications: RRL's individual risk factors and NLN's interactions can provide complementary insight; unseen attacks complicate interpretation of NSL-KDD generalization; and NLN/LAD rule counts are not directly equivalent because their rules differ in expressiveness. The causal-interpretation discussion moved from Appendix B.3 to Section 2.4 is retained content.

D1.justification: v3 adds a Code Availability statement and repository address. Appendix D.2.1 documents RRL merging, averaging output biases, successive pruning, and absorbing empty-rule contributions into biases. These add reproducibility information without revising the existing NLN implementation description.

R1.justification: v3 adds references by Klement, Kitainik, Ruspini, Kumar and Das, and Tavallaee and colleagues. It distinguishes its fuzzy dichotomies from earlier terminology and expands its positioning relative to LAD's scalability and rule expressiveness. The main related-work discussion remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The overall section structure and most prose are retained. Local changes clarify the logical-program explanation and terminology, move causal-interpretation prose into the main text, express the existing kidney rules in text, expand the conclusion, and introduce application appendix subsections.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 6–7, the merged RRL display in Figure 7, class-coverage plots in Figure 8, and 24 rule diagrams in Appendix D.3.1. Existing displays are also repositioned. Figure 6 changes AND/OR symbols to intersection/union symbols while retaining its rules and thresholds. The new comparative and analytical displays substantially expand the visual evidence.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's NLN-only medical case, v3 supplies a simplified RRL counterpart and a more balanced interpretation, plus industrial generalization/transfer evidence and code-access information. These provide a limited overall gain. Reporting remains imperfect: Table 4's revised RRL mean of 313.6 tic-tac-toe rules is not reconciled with the retained claim that the smallest model has 318 rules.
